If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid overconfidence bias.  
If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (days 1–5) to compensate for pessimism.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00 on day 1 of forecast window, reduce forecast by 2–3% for the first 3 days to reflect market overreaction.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast in late horizon (days 20–30) to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is mixed and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast in late horizon to avoid lagging correction.  
If sentiment is 0.00 or 1.00 on day 1 and forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce forecast by 3–5% in first 5 days to prevent overfitting.
